newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-REAL MADRID BOOSTED BY CONVINCING WIN OVER SPORTING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-REAL MADRID BOOSTED BY CONVINCING WIN OVER SPORTING.

text.p: Real Madrid shook off their internal problems and an early goal from Sporting Gijon to score a convincing 3-1 Spanish league win on Sunday.

Davor Suker ended his goal drought to find the net twice, and set-piece specialist Roberto Carlos thundered home another as Real took a provisional 11-point lead over Barcelona, who play Extremadura on Monday.
Throughout the game Real fans shouted insults at coach Fabio Capello, who five days earlier announced his decision to leave the club at the end of the season.
The Real board on Saturday appealed for unity in the wake of the upheaval caused by Capello's announcement.
The conflict initially seemed to have unnerved the Real players, who went behind to a ninth-minute goal.
But Suker pounced on a deflected clearance shortly before half-time and there was no stopping Real in the second half as their opponents were reduced to 10 men.
"We needed the win with everything that has happened," said Suker's striker partner Predrag Mijatovic.

In other games, Real Betis lost steam by drawing their third consecutive home game. The goalless draw with Compostela left Betis in third, level on points with Barcelona and fourth-placed Deportivo Coruna, who beat Sevilla 3-0 on Saturday.

International striker Kiko Narvaez squandered a penalty and a late chance as reigning champions Atletico Madrid drew 1-1 at Racing Santander, while Tenerife scored a last-minute goal to beat Rayo Vallecano 2-1.
Two other UEFA Cup hopefuls, Athletic Bilbao and Valladolid played out a goalless draw, while Valencia were held 1-1 by Celta Vigo.
